item.title: Spectral unions of intervals with few rational relation tile the real line
item.description: arXiv:2611.00307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every spectral finite union of pairwise disjoint bounded intervals whose lengths satisfy at most four linearly independent rational relations tiles the real line, and that each of its spectra has at most five cosets modulo its least period. This includes every spectral union of at most five bounded intervals. The proof combines specialization preserving subset-sum equalities with rigidity of exchanges between finite spectral fibers. We also obtain common tiling complements for all spectra of primitive sets of at most seven elements in finite cyclic groups, and establish the sharp eleven-point range in which consecutive pairs force periodicity of the dual set.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Okezue Bell

item.title: Spectral Theory and Continuum Norm Resolvent Convergence of a One-Sided Discrete Dirac-Type Operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.00820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a one-dimensional discrete Dirac-type operator $D_d$ acting on the Hilbert space $\big(\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$, obtained from the classical continuous free Dirac operator by replacing the spatial derivative with the one-sided backward difference operator $I - S_1$, where $S_1$ denotes the right shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})$. We establish the fundamental operator-theoretic and spectral properties of $D_d$: unlike symmetric or supersymmetric lattice discretizations, $D_d$ is bounded and non-normal for every non-zero rest mass $m > 0$, with self-commutator $[D_d, D_d^\dag] = -2mc^3(-\Delta_{\mathrm{disc}})\sigma_2$, yet it is quadratically normal. We compute the exact operator norm, determine the exact spectral radius in two mass regimes, and show via Fourier--Laurent analysis that the spectrum $\sigma(D_d)$ is purely continuous and lies on a two-component algebraic curve in the complex plane undergoing a topological transition at $mc^2 = 2c$. Finally, introducing a lattice spacing $h > 0$ and embedding $\big(\ell^2(h\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ isometrically into $\big(L^2(\mathbb{R};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ via Whittaker--Shannon band-limited interpolation, we prove that the scaled non-normal discrete Dirac-type operator $D_{d,h}$ converges to the continuous self-adjoint Dirac operator $D$ in the norm resolvent sense at the optimal rate $\mathcal{O}(h)$ as $h \to 0^+$, without requiring frequency cutoffs.
item.dc:creator: Mariusz Niwi\'nski

item.title: Two-scale estimates for limit-periodic Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.01303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional continuum Schr\"odinger operators by comparing the spectral geometry at two consecutive periods. Enlarging a period decomposes each fiber into the eigenspaces of translation by the smaller cell. Away from the larger-period symmetry momenta, a simple ordered band remains in one translation sector and agrees with one translated smaller-period band. This permits us to combine large-period ordering and non-overlap with a smaller-period derivative bound. We obtain lower bounds for folded band widths and confine all near-collisions to a common neighborhood of the symmetry momenta, with the exponential cost at the smaller period. For nested periods $p_n$ with $p_{n+1}/p_n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p_{n+1}\ge2p_n$, approximation errors $o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-\eta p_n})$, where $\eta>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, give a nonzero strong asymptotic velocity on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. Every position moment of order $0<r\le4$ has two-sided ballistic growth. A period-uniform form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a linear dynamical comparison complete the argument. No upper bound on successive period ratios is assumed, and the sufficient approximation exponents are not claimed to be optimal.
item.dc:creator: Moises Gomez Solis

item.title: An affine reverse Faber-Krahn inequality via information decay
item.description: arXiv:2611.02279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ admits $S\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ such that $\lambda_1(SK)|K|^{2/n}\le Cn$, where $C$ is universal. For origin-symmetric bodies of volume one, the bound holds in maximal Gaussian measure position. The main step is the spectral estimate \[ \lambda_1(D)\le C(P)\bigl(n+\sqrt{n I(\nu\mid\gamma_n)}\bigr) \] for an even isotropic log-concave probability measure $\nu$ supported on a symmetric convex body $D$, with Poincar\'e constant at most $P$ and finite relative Fisher information. A second-order Stein estimate and an information jump under convolution give entropy decay faster than $m^{-1}$ for normalised sums. Their supports control the Gaussian measure of dilates, and a Brownian bridge expansion gives the spectral estimate. A Gaussian-weighted ground state supplies a measure whose Fisher information is bounded in terms of $\lambda_1(K)$. The square-root dependence then gives the bound of order $n$.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Colbrook, George Stepaniants

item.title: Estimates for Ratios of Low-Order Eigenvalues of the Laplacian with Muckenhoupt Weights on Euclidean Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.02701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study low-order eigenvalue ratio estimates for the Laplacian with Muckenhoupt $A_2$ weights. For weights bounded above and below, we prove a universal upper bound for $\lambda_2/\lambda_1$ with constant $1 + \frac{4}{n}\,\frac{C}{c}$, linear in the ratio of the weight bounds, and recover the classical Payne-P\'{o}lya-Weinberger bound as a special case. For radial decreasing weights, we prove that the ball maximizes $\lambda_2/\lambda_1$ among domains of equal volume, assuming that an admissible radial test function exists (Definition 5.8) and that on the ball the second eigenvalue is attained by the $l=1$ mode. The argument adapts the method of Ashbaugh--Benguria to the weighted setting via a weighted Chiti comparison theorem and a monotonicity property of the admissible radial test function (Definition 5.8). Higher-order eigenvalue ratios are estimated in terms of the $(n-1)$-Hausdorff measure of the boundary, under an explicit balance condition on the weight at the covering scale. The generalized Payne-P\'{o}lya-Weinberger conjecture for eigenvalue sums remains open in general; conditional results are presented for restricted families of domains.
item.dc:creator: Jing Mao, He-Jun Sun, Lingzhong Zeng

item.title: Edge spectral invariants and second-order Steklov asymptotics for the regular tetrahedron
item.description: arXiv:2611.02733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a two-term Weyl asymptotic for the Steklov spectrum of a solid regular tetrahedron. Its linear coefficient is the total edge length times an explicit, absolutely convergent dihedral invariant. A trace-class difference of massive Neumann-to-Dirichlet operators computes the full invariant, including the continuous spectrum. The main analytic step is a fixed-time cumulative trace comparison between the compact tetrahedron and its exact half-space or dihedral models. Localized Hilbert-Schmidt defects have vanishing high-energy tails; retaining the time factor in Duhamel's formula makes this sufficient for an $o(L)$ cumulative error. A separate trace-class face comparison fixes the model's infinite exterior primitive and permits one observation time independent of the inner collar width. Compact-band Mourre estimates and a harmonic comparison establish immediate reflection/transmission support for incident face waves. Triangular unfolding gives null periodic and dead-end sets for the maximal branching relation. Actual edge-window bounds, adapted conical annuli and an ordered-limit Fourier-Tauberian argument then prove the sharp remainder. The proof treats guided and continuum channels together in the edge trace and requires neither a guided metric graph nor a lower-departure estimate uniform at zero tangential momentum.
item.dc:creator: Josiah Park

item.title: Inferring geometric structure from eigenfunction triple products
item.description: arXiv:2611.03619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents two converses to well-known observations regarding products of eigenfunctions of the Laplacian on a closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$. First, if $(M,g)$ is real-analytic, the coefficients in the eigenfunction expansion of a product of eigenfunctions decay exponentially. We show that such exponential decay in fact implies that $g$ is real-analytic. Second, it is clear that if $(M,g)$ is flat, there exists an eigenbasis for which the product of any two of its elements lies in the span of at most $N = N(M,g)$ elements. We prove that any manifold with such an eigenbasis must be flat. We then construct metrics on $\mathbb{S}^7$ that share an eigenbasis with the standard metric yet are not locally homogeneous, from which we deduce that homogeneity cannot be characterized solely in terms of the multiplicative structure of eigenfunctions.
item.dc:creator: Josef Greilhuber, Romain Speciel

item.title: A Preconditioned Semismooth Newton Method for Box-Constrained Elliptic Optimal Control Problems with Random Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.00246v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the optimal control problem of an elliptic PDE with random diffusion under pointwise box constraints on the control. The constraints make the optimality conditions nonsmooth, with an active set that is not known in advance, and the random diffusion couples the state and the adjoint across all stochastic modes. To design a solution algorithm for this problem, we rely on the Fenchel duality viewpoint. Fenchel duality absorbs the box constraint into the objective and yields an exact reduced problem in the elliptic adjoint variable alone. After a stochastic Galerkin--finite element discretization, eliminating the state leaves a strongly monotone, piecewise smooth equation, which we solve directly by a matrix-free semismooth Newton method with the box projection retained exactly and with no outer iteration, penalty or smoothing parameter. Next, we introduce and analyze a current-set preconditioner, which adds the active-set correction of the current Newton step to a mean-diffusion reference operator and is inverted exactly by a rank-1 update. For implementation, we use a cheaper preconditioner that keeps only a fraction of free control values. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence of the state, and Newton and PCG counts that stay bounded under mesh refinement and growth of the stochastic dimension.
item.dc:creator: Zhendong Li, Akwum Onwunta, Hailing Wang

item.title: Bilateral Christoffel-Geronimus-Uvarov formulas for mixed-type orthogonality on algebraic supports
item.description: arXiv:2611.00457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Christoffel-type determinant formulas construct both normalized polynomial families and their reproducing kernel for mixed-type orthogonality in several variables after independent rational matrix transformations on the two arguments. The pairing may have a rectangular matrix of functionals, with separate degree bounds on each component, and may be supported on an algebraic variety. The reduced matrices are calculated from the original biorthogonal polynomials, rational moments, polynomial division and the masses left free by division; their nonvanishing determinants characterize existence and uniqueness. For measure pairings the rational data are expressed by Cauchy and multivariate Fantappie transforms. Exact dimension counts incorporate the four matrix factors and the relations of the support. For normal degree-ordered original families and fixed factors, when the component degrees on each side differ by a bounded amount and the normalization dimension grows at most like one degree layer, the resulting orders are bounded on curves and grow at most linearly on surfaces. For pairings allowing scalar factors to move between arguments, called balanced pairings, an exact obstruction determines whether a bilateral mass decomposes into unilateral masses when the denominators act injectively. Residue duality provides coordinates for division and mass quotients on integral curves, including singular points, and on the finite surface quotients specified here. Explicit singular-curve families retain nondegenerate residue pairings as denominator zeros coalesce. Positive congruences admit a further reduction by orthogonal projection, while balanced pairings give simultaneous intertwining identities for all coordinate multiplication matrices.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Ma\~nas

item.title: Spectral and convex geometry of $\alpha$-harmonic maps and sharp Morse index rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.00642v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a weighted scalar spectral geometric description of Sacks-Uhlenbeck $\alpha$-harmonic maps into round spheres and identify its convex geometry realization for $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphisms onto the round $2$-sphere. More precisely, we establish a one-to-one correspondence, modulo orientation preserving isometries of $\mathbb{S}^2$, between orientation preserving $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphisms onto the round $2$-sphere and positive Codazzi tensors satisfying a determinant bound and a compatibility condition with the prescribed metric on $\mathbb{S}^2$. These tensors are the radii tensors of auxiliary strictly convex surfaces, and the weighted scalar forms in spectral geometry equal $-\alpha$ times the second variations of the enclosed volumes with respect to the support functions. Using these spectral geometry and convex geometry results, we prove a sharp Morse index characterization of isometric equatorial parametrizations among $\alpha$-harmonic $2$-spheres in the round $n$-sphere. We also prove that every $\alpha$-harmonic diffeomorphism between unit round $2$-spheres is orthogonal for all $\alpha>1$. Equivalently, the only admissible positive Codazzi tensor whose reconstructed metric on $\mathbb{S}^2$ has Gaussian curvature $1$ is $(\kappa+2)^{\alpha-1}\bar{g}$, where $\bar{g}$ is the unit round metric.
item.dc:creator: Rui Gao, Miaomiao Zhu

item.title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.00703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(\mathcal T_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal A$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Ces\`aro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the $e$-property, the Jacobs--de Leeuw--Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi--Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner--Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Ces\`aro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Projection-face criteria are treated in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kania, Mariusz Niwi\'nski

item.title: Congruent quotient matrix, nodal domain, and nodal count
item.description: arXiv:2611.00789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the congruent quotient matrix along with its inequalities on inertia and demonstrate that these inequalities are the essence of the discrete nodal domain theorem, the bounds on nodal counts, and Fiedler's characterization on tree eigenvectors. Using these techniques, we also extend the existing bounds for the number of nodal domains and nodal counts.
item.dc:creator: Jephian C. -H. Lin

item.title: Non-backtracking Laplacian for hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.01121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the non-backtracking Laplacian for graphs, introduced by Jost, Mulas and Torres, to hypergraphs. The operator is defined on the permutations of the edges and is normalized by the number of edges through which a non-backtracking walk can continue. We show that it satisfies a symmetry that generalizes the graph case, and that it can be obtained from the random walk Laplacian of a directed graph by rescaling if and only if all edges have the same cardinality. Moreover, we show that, up to copies of the eigenvalue $1$, its spectrum can be computed from a much smaller matrix indexed by the incidences of the hypergraph, and we use this reduction to bound the remaining eigenvalues away from $1$.
item.dc:creator: Eleonora Andreotti, Raffaella Mulas

item.title: Functions of $\boldsymbol{S}_p$-almost commuting unitary operators and contractions. An extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.01149v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study functions of pairs of unitary operators and pairs of contractions with commutators in the Schatten-von Neumann class $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. We obtain commutator estimates and prove that our functional calculus is multiplicative modulo $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. On the other hand, we show that our commutator estimates do not extend to the case $p>2$. We also obtain an extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula. The main tool of this paper is a technique of triple operator integrals.
item.dc:creator: A. B. Aleksandrov, V. V. Peller

item.title: Perfectness of partial Christoffel transforms of Nikishin systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01395v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study multiple orthogonal polynomial systems obtained from a Nikishin system of two measures by applying a Christoffel transform to one of the measures at a point $x=x_0$. We show that if $x_0$ separates the supports of the generating measures, then the modified systems remain perfect. As an application, we prove that the type I multiple orthogonal polynomials of a Nikishin system have no zeros in the gap between the supports of its generating measures.
item.dc:creator: Rostyslav Kozhan

item.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
item.description: arXiv:2611.01503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain a complete bound independent of the two disks, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.
item.dc:creator: Mihai Putinar, Georgios Tsikalas

item.title: The real eigenvalues of the non-backtracking Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2611.02194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $N$ nodes and $M$ edges, with minimum degree at least $2$. We prove that the non-backtracking Laplacian of $G$ has at least $2M-2N+2c+2b$ real eigenvalues, counted with algebraic multiplicity, where $c$ is the number of connected components of $G$ and $b$ is the number of bipartite ones. More precisely, at least $M-N+2c$ of them lie in $[0,1)$ and at least $M-N+2b$ lie in $(1,2]$. We show that the bound $2M-2N+2c+2b$ is sharp, and that a connected $d$-regular graph attains it if and only if it is strictly Ramanujan, i.e., every adjacency eigenvalue $\mu\ne\pm d$ satisfies $|\mu|<2\sqrt{d-1}$. For completeness, we also show that the non-backtracking Laplacian has at most $2M-2c-2b$ real eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Raffaella Mulas, Leo Torres

item.title: How the eigenvalue region of standardized Laplacians leaves the 2005 polygon
item.description: arXiv:2611.02249v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of $n\times n$ standardized Laplacian matrices, and let $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ be the polygon introduced in 2005, with upper vertices $\lambda_0=0,\dots,\lambda_{n-1}=1$. It is now known that $\Lambda_n=S_n$, and that $\Lambda_n$ is convex, if and only if $n\le4$. We study how $\Lambda_n$ leaves $S_n$ near an edge $[\lambda_m,\lambda_{m+1}]$, $2(m+1)<n$. First, we prove a switching law for matrices having a boundary point of $\Lambda_n$ as a simple eigenvalue: an explicit switching function on the arcs, built from the left and right eigenvectors and the outward normal, forces maximal weight where positive and zero weight where negative; intermediate weights occur only where it vanishes. Second, we perturb the weights of the arcs $k\to k+m+1$ in the circulant digraph (arcs $k\to k+s$, $1\le s\le m$, plus these arcs with weight $\tau$) that realizes the point $\lambda_m+\tau(\lambda_{m+1}-\lambda_m)$. At second order, the first Fourier harmonic of the perturbation moves the eigenvalue beyond the line of the edge if and only if $\tau<\tau^*_m=\sin(\pi m/n)/(2\cos(\pi/n)\sin(\pi(m+1)/n))$. For even $n$ and $m$, the point with $\tau=\tau^*_m$ is the vertex of $S_{n/2}$ lying on this edge, and digraphs with these arcs only at even $k$ give an explicit eigenvalue path that leaves $S_n$ at $\lambda_m$ and, in all computed cases, ends at this vertex. Third, we give a conjectural, numerically supported picture of $\partial\Lambda_5$: beyond each edge of $S_5$ not incident to $0$ or $1$, $\Lambda_5$ forms a cap bounded by four algebraic arcs, which leaves the edge tangentially at its endpoint adjacent to $0$ or $1$ and rejoins it at $\tau^*_1=(3-\sqrt5)/2$; the rest of the edge lies on $\partial\Lambda_5$. In computations for $n\le8$, a cap returns to its edge smoothly at $\tau^*_m$, at a corner at $\tau^*_m$, or at a corner beyond $\tau^*_m$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Chebotarev

item.title: Joint Moments of Bilinear Resolvents
item.description: arXiv:2611.03081v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given $A,B\in B\left(H\right)_{+}$, we consider the existence and uniqueness of a positive operator $C\in B\left(H\right)_{+}$ such that \[ \left(I+mA+nB+mnC\right)^{-1}=\int_{\left[0,1\right]^{2}}s^{m}t^{n}dE\left(s,t\right),\quad m,n\geq0, \] for a positive operator-valued measure $E$. This is a joint Hausdorff moment problem. Without $C$, it holds if and only if $AB=BA$. In dimension two we give a complete criterion for noncommuting pairs. In higher finite dimensions, nonexistence is generic. Under certain spectral and cyclicity assumptions, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition on arbitrary Hilbert spaces. The completion is unique in this case. We also classify these pairs up to unitary equivalence. The class includes irreducible infinite-dimensional examples, even with continuous spectrum.
item.dc:creator: James Tian

item.title: On a polygon version of Wiegmann-Zabrodin formula
item.description: arXiv:2503.13718v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $P$ be a convex polygon in ${\mathbb C}$ and let $\Delta_{D, P}$ be the operator of the Dirichlet boundary value problem for the Lapalcian $\Delta=-4\partial_z\partial_{\bar z}$ in $P$. We derive a variational formula for the logarithm of the $\zeta$-regularized determinant of $\Delta_{D, P}$ for arbitrary infinitesimal deformations of the polygon $P$ in the class of polygons (with the same number of vertices). For a simply connected domain with smooth boundary such a formula was recently discovered by Wiegmann and Zabrodin as a non obvious corollary of the Alvarez variational formula, for domains with corners this approach is unavailable (at least for those deformations that do not preserve the corner angles) and we have to develop another one.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Kokotov, Dmitrii Korikov

item.title: Inequalities between Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues in large dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2606.30120v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded domain in $R^d$. Denote by $\lambda_k$ (resp. $\mu_k$) the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator in $\Omega$ with Dirichlet (resp. Neumann) boundary conditions. Denote by $\Psi = \Psi (d,k,\Omega)$ the shift of indices in the inequality $\mu_{k+\Psi} \le \lambda_k$. We are interested to describe the behaviour of $\Psi$ for large $d$. We prove that a) $\Psi (d,1,\Omega) \ge C (e/2)^d$ for all domains $\Omega$; and b) $\Psi (d,k,\Omega) \ge C (e/2)^d$ for all $k$ and all convex domains $\Omega$.
item.dc:creator: N. Filonov

item.title: A Direct Polynomial Approach to Spectral Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2607.20218v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a direct construction of the spectral projectors of a complex square matrix, based on explicit interpolation polynomials previously introduced. This yields a spectral resolution $A=\sum_{i=1}^r(\lambda_iP_i+N_i)$ from which the Primary Decomposition Theorem, the Cayley--Hamilton theorem, criteria for diagonalizability, and the spectral theorem for normal matrices are proved by short formal arguments. A weaker form of the construction, extends to any perfect fields via a Galois invariance argument and produces the Jordan--Chevalley decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Simon Bossoney, Marc Troyanov

item.title: Smooth perturbation theory and generic Cantor spectrum for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.00733v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider multi-dimensional quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators with monotone sawtooth-type potentials in the perturbative localization regime. We prove that a given gap is closed iff a corresponding (via a natural gap labeling) eigenfunction vanishes at the origin. Using this, we show that for a generic choice of the sampling function $f$, the spectrum of such an operator is a Cantor set, with all possible gaps being open. We also provide a class of functions $f$ for which some gaps are closed. Finally, we observe that certain gaps are more difficult to close than the others.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Kachkovskiy, Leonid Parnovski, Roman Shterenberg

item.title: Use of bundles of locally convex spaces in problems of convergence of semigroups of operators defined on different Banach spaces. Applications to spectral stability problems
item.description: arXiv:0906.2953v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work we construct certain general bundles $<\mathfrak{M},\rho,X>$ and $<\mathfrak{B},\eta,X>$ of Hausdorff locally convex spaces associated with a given Banach bundle $<\mathfrak{E},\pi,X>$. Then we present conditions ensuring the existence of bounded sections $\mathcal{U}\in \Gamma^{x_{\infty}}(\rho)$ and $\mathcal{P}\in \Gamma^{x_{\infty}}(\eta)$ both continuous at a point $x_{\infty}\in X$, such that $\mathcal{U}(x)$ is a $C_{0}-$semigroup of contractions on $\mathfrak{E}_{x}$ and $\mathcal{P}(x)$ is a spectral projector of the infinitesimal generator of the semigroup $\mathcal{U}(x)$, for every $x\in X$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Eurasian Math. J. 7,3 (2016) 53-88; Eurasian Math. J. 7,4 (2016) 46-78; Eurasian Math. J. 8,3 (2017) 85-108
item.dc:creator: Benedetto Silvestri

item.title: Effective eigenvalue approximation from moments for self-adjoint trace-class operators
item.description: arXiv:2407.04478v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spectral properties of bounded linear operators play a crucial role in several areas of mathematics and physics. For each self-adjoint, trace-class operator $O$ we define a set $\Lambda_n\subset \mathbb{R}$, and we show that it converges to the spectrum of $O$ in the Hausdorff metric under mild conditions. Our set $\Lambda_n$ only depends on the first $n$ moments of $O$. We show that it can be effectively calculated for physically relevant operators, and it approximates the spectrum well without diagonalization. We prove that using the above method we can converge to the minimal and maximal eigenvalues with super-exponential speed. We also construct monotone increasing lower bounds $q_n$ for the minimal eigenvalue (or decreasing upper bounds for the maximal eigenvalue). This sequence only depends on the moments of $O$ and a concrete upper estimate of its $1$-norm; we also demonstrate that $q_n$ can be effectively calculated for a large class of physically relevant operators. This rigorous lower bound $q_n$ tends to the minimal eigenvalue with super-exponential speed provided that $O$ is not positive semidefinite. As a by-product, we obtain computable upper bounds for the $1$-norm of $O$, too. Numerical examples demonstrate the relevance of our approximation in estimating entropy and negativity, which is useful, among others, in quantum optical and in open quantum system models. The results can be directly applicable to problems in quantum information, statistical mechanics, and quantum thermodynamics, where using traditional techniques based on diagonalization is impractical.
item.dc:creator: Rich\'ard Balka, G\'abor Homa, Andr\'as Csord\'as

item.title: Low-Rank Denoising for Predict-then-Optimize
item.description: arXiv:2609.15111v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A shortest-path decision is often made from edge costs that are only observed through noisy samples, such as the average of $m$ simulation replications. When the mean cost vectors of different instances lie near a $k$-dimensional subspace, projecting the averaged sample onto that subspace should remove noise. We make this precise. The mean squared error of any projection estimator splits exactly into a variance term and a bias term. The best projector is the positive eigenspace of $\Sigma_c - D/m$, where $\Sigma_c$ is the covariance of the true costs and $D$ is the noise covariance. For a rank-$k$ signal, the projection has the error of a sample mean with a factor $d/(\mu k)$ more replications, where $d$ is the number of edges and $\mu$ is an incoherence constant. For a signal that is only approximately low-rank, every rank-$k$ projection has an error floor, and the plain average wins beyond an explicit replication count. A margin bound shows that the chance of choosing a suboptimal path falls at the same improved rate. A projector learned from $n$ noisy instances loses at most an $O(d/n)$ term.
item.dc:creator: Henry Aldridge-Krawciw, Irene Aldridge

item.title: Effective atom-dimer bands of three-body lattice systems at strong coupling: exact critical mass ratios and a statistics-quasimomentum duality
item.description: arXiv:2609.33576v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study three particles on the two-dimensional square lattice with contact interactions of infinite strength, in every sector of total quasimomentum, for three statistics: identical bosons, two identical fermions with a distinguishable third particle, and two identical bosons with a distinguishable third particle. The atom-dimer sector associated with the infinitely degenerate eigenvalue of the pair-contact operator is analysed on the whole Brillouin zone. A Feshbach-Schur reduction gives explicit effective Hamiltonians built from the Dirichlet Laplacian and a rank-four exchange operator, and a spectral transfer theorem with explicit error bounds identifies the atom-dimer threshold of the three-body operator with that of the effective one; the eigenvalue counting function below the threshold is squeezed between those of the effective operator, so that the number of atom-dimer states bound uniformly in the coupling equals the number of bound states of the effective Hamiltonian. The threshold problem reduces to a four-by-four Hermitian matrix whose zero-energy limit is built from the two-point resistances of the square lattice and hence to a quartic polynomial. This yields the complete atom-dimer zones in closed form; the critical hopping ratio as an explicit function on the whole Brillouin zone with two-sided bounds and closed forms at all symmetry points; at most two atom-dimer states per sector with an explicit second threshold; exact onset laws of infinite order at the corner point and linear-over-logarithmic in the pure p-wave channel; and two exact dualities relating a change of statistics to a shift of quasimomentum by half a reciprocal-lattice vector. The reduction of the three-body eigenvalue problem to the lattice Skornyakov-Ter-Martirosyan equation is proved with an explicit isomorphism of eigenspaces.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail V. Dolgopolov

item.title: Positive Bidiagonal Factorizations and Mixed-Type Chebyshev Multiple Orthogonal Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.08568v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterize when a semi-infinite banded totally positive matrix admits a positive bidiagonal factorization, without assuming boundedness, and establish criteria for stability under perturbations. These criteria distinguish whether the initial factor entries are fixed or allowed to vary. For banded totally positive Toeplitz matrices, such factorizations always exist; a factorization can be chosen to depend analytically on all sufficiently small perturbations within the same band if and only if the polynomial symbol has distinct roots. Explicit root formulas determine the associated mixed-type multiple orthogonal polynomials and their matrix of positive measures. They also yield scalar linear forms independent of the chosen factorization, from which we obtain asymptotic zero spacing and sine-kernel limits. We further treat finite boundary modifications and limiting zero distributions for matrices with convergent diagonals.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Ma\~nas

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28391v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: The sharp leading asymptotics of the self-energy of the spinless Pauli-Fierz model
item.description: arXiv:2610.34122v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the self-energy $E_0(\alpha,\Lambda)$ of the spinless Pauli-Fierz model with a sharp ultraviolet cutoff $\Lambda$, retaining the vacuum contribution of the $A^2$ term (no normal ordering); $\alpha=e^2/4\pi$ is the fine structure constant. Lieb and Loss proved lower and upper bounds of orders $\alpha^{1/2}\Lambda^{3/2}$ and $\alpha^{2/7}\Lambda^{12/7}$ for large $\Lambda$ and suggested that the upper bound, which comes from product states, gives the correct order. We prove that, for every fixed $\alpha>0$, $E_0(\alpha,\Lambda)=(1+o(1))\,c_\alpha\,\alpha^{2/7}\Lambda^{12/7}$, with an explicit constant $c_\alpha=0.99338\ldots$, as $\Lambda\to\infty$. The same asymptotics hold uniformly in the joint limit $\Lambda/\alpha\to\infty$, $\alpha^{5/2}\Lambda\to\infty$, provided $\log(2+\alpha)=o((\Lambda/\alpha)^{1/21})$. The infimum of the energy over product states has the same leading asymptotics. The upper bound follows from a coherent state bound for the field energy in a fixed electron density. For the lower bound we combine a periodization of the field, a blockwise Born-Oppenheimer bound, and a lower bound on the magnetic Neumann Laplacian on a cube for band-limited fields. The magnetic estimate follows from a non-concentration bound for the vorticity of band-limited fields satisfying a weighted gradient condition.
item.dc:creator: Shinichiro Futakuchi

item.title: The effective mass of the Pauli-Fierz electron: a cutoff-independent lower bound and the breakdown of mass renormalization
item.description: arXiv:2610.34125v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the effective mass of a spinless non-relativistic electron coupled to the quantized transverse electromagnetic field (the Pauli-Fierz model without external potential), with bare mass $m$, fine structure constant $\alpha=e^2/4\pi$ and a sharp ultraviolet cutoff $\Lambda$. We define $1/(2m_{\rm eff}):=\limsup_{P\to0}(E(P)-E(0))/|P|^2$ for the fiber ground state energy $E(P)$; this agrees with the curvature mass whenever $E$ is twice differentiable at zero. By scaling, $h=m_{\rm eff}/m$ depends only on $\alpha$ and $\lambda=\Lambda/m$. For all $\alpha>0$ and $\lambda\ge1$ we prove $h\ge1+0.3441\,\alpha/(1+0.2985\sqrt\alpha+0.1252\,\alpha)$, a bound independent of the cutoff; with the band extended to the cutoff, its first order coefficient in $\alpha$ is the perturbative one of Hiroshima and Spohn. At fixed $\alpha>0$ we further prove $h\ge\lambda^{8/7-\epsilon}$ for every $\epsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $\lambda$. Hence $\iota_{\rm PF}(\alpha):=\inf_{\lambda>0}h/\lambda>0$: at fixed coupling, a bare mass reproducing a prescribed physical mass $m_{\rm phys}$ can exist only if $\Lambda\le m_{\rm phys}/\iota_{\rm PF}(\alpha)$. This proves the obstruction to mass renormalization at fixed physical mass anticipated by Lieb and Loss (2002). The first bound uses a coherent translation of the field applied to the ground state as a trial state. The second uses the sharp self-energy asymptotics of a companion paper and a position estimator constructed from the local centre of a shallow level set of the photon cloud.
item.dc:creator: Shinichiro Futakuchi
